chapter: Meeting Jay McShann and Martin's on the Plaza
title: McShann's money: royalties, garbage trucks and investments
summary: Dance and Ramey discuss how McShann made money, including garbage trucks and royalties.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Well, somebody said that he was sort of comfortably off now. Well, where did he get that money from?
Mostly from the royalties, and those jobs out there.
He saved some money in those days.
Oh, yeah. I remember one time it was hard on him, he had some garbage trucks. He had three or four garbage trucks that were going around picking up garbage, and he had to hire the guys doing that.
Oh, he's got a business head then?
Yeah, evidently. He had that for a few years until his music started getting back going, you know. And at the same time he had records all over.

Yeah, but I never thought he that would have made much from his records. I mean, he made something from those things like, you know, when "Confessin' the Blues" came out, and he sold a half a million, they say.
Yeah. Well, he -- I don't know where else he got it, but he's up there with a whole lots of those guys.
Yeah. Well, you never know, do you, really. I mean, I know --

He confides in me, and on this trip to Europe he was telling me about how he got his money -- I won't say the amounts, but he's got amounts spread in different places, because before his wife passed, it seemed like he was going to have problems, or something. And judging from what he's saying about the amounts, and he wanted me to advise him on whether he should invest in this or that, and everything, I said, even a stockbroker's not going to advise you to do that, and I'm not a broker, you know.
